newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia signs 25 mln ECU loan with EIB, sees more.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia signs 25 mln ECU loan with EIB, sees more.

text.p: Slovakia on Friday signed a 25 million ECU, nine-year loan with the European Investment Bank (EIB) for motorway construction.
The interest rate was set at 15 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) with credit payments starting in 2003 and complete repayment by 2012.
Slovak Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik and EIB Vice- President Wolfgang Roth also signed a framework agreeement on EIB loan activities in Slovakia over the next three years.
"The agreement foresees EIB loans of some 100 million ECU a year in Slovakia between 1997 and 1999," Kozlik told a news conference after a signing ceremony.
The 25 million ECU loan will mostly finance new routes between the Slovak capital Bratislava and the Austrian and Hungarian borders.
Loans extended under the framework agreement should also go to other infrastructure projects such as further developing the mobile telephone network.
The EIB is the European Union's long-term credit arm focusing on financing infrastructure programmes in post- communist European countries.
Roth said the EIB wanted to intensify its credit activities in Slovakia, adding it intended to provide loans in the local currency, the crown.
"We plan to extend crown credits with longer maturities of between five to 10 years," Roth said.

Asked if Slovakia's exclusion from the first wave of countries expected to be invited to accession talks with the EU will have a negative influence on Bratislava's cooperation with the EIB, Roth said "the Slovak government has said it wants the country integrated to the EU, and that is the base for us.

"The bank has no political opinion, but it surely has an opinion on how the European motorway network should be built and how it should be financed. So, we will continue to finance infrastructure projects in countries that applied for EU membership," Roth said.
The EIB has extended ECU 378 million loans to Slovakia since 1993, financing mainly motorway and gas pipeline construction and upgrading the telecommunication network and energy sector.
